(1) the levels of CaPB in dentate gyrus granule cells are regulated in response to kindling and are not affected by adrenalectomy, hypophysectomy or ischemia; (2) the levels of PV in the dentate are regulated in response hypophysectomy but not kindling; (3) PV is a useful marker for a subpopulation of dentate GABAergic neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

CaBP is an indicator of the development of granule cells but is not involved in their susceptibility to kindling or ischemia, while PV is an indicator of development of a subpopulation within the granule cell population and is regulated by the endocrine system.
CaBP is a marker for granule cells and PV is a marker for GABAergic neurons in the dentate hilus and that the levels of both proteins are regulated by hormones.
the CaBP and PV systems are not involved in the regulation of seizure susceptibility or the effects of kindling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CaBP and PV are not useful as markers of neuronal vulnerability to ischemic injury in adult rats.
the calcium-binding proteins, calbindin and parvalbumin, are useful markers for the development and maturation of dentate granule and GABAergic cells.
CaBP and PV are both useful markers for specific cell populations in the dentate granule cell layer, but they are not useful as markers for the effects of ischemic or kindling injury.
